For in this way, the unique qualities of a Buddha do not grasp at the unique qualities of a Buddha. For in this way, Venerable Śāriputra, there is no grasping at omniscience. Why is that?
Because omniscience does not grasp at omniscience, based on everything from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence.
For it is for the sake of the non-grasping of all phenomena, Venerable Śāriputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva [practices].
"He trains in omniscience; he will emerge into omniscience.
Śāriputra said:
"Venerable Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who trains in this way trains in the perfection of wisdom; he will emerge into omniscience."
Subhūti said:
"Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in this way trains in the perfection of wisdom and will emerge into omniscience through the yoga of non-appropriation of all dharmas. Thus it was said;
then Śāriputra spoke regarding that very point:
“Venerable Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way—having trained for the sake of neither grasping nor the disappearance of all dharmas—how will he go forth to omniscience?
Subhūti replied:
“For in that way, Venerable Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva courses in the perfection of wisdom, he does not perceive the arising of form.”
He perceives neither cessation nor grasping, neither relinquishment nor defilement, neither purification nor accumulation, nor diminution, neither decrease nor increase. For what reason?
Because, venerable Śāriputra, form does not exist by way of its own intrinsic nature (rūpasvabhāva).

Venerable Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the arising or the cessation of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; nor does he perceive their grasping or relinquishing, their defilement or purification, their increase or decrease, nor their loss or growth. Why is that?

For indeed, venerable Śāriputra, consciousness does not exist by way of its own-being as consciousness. In this same way, the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields— whether taken individually or collectively— the factors of dependent origination, the perfections, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, the formless attainments, the superknowledges, all the concentrations, and all the doors of the dhāraṇīs [do not exist by way of their own-being].

He does not perceive the arising or the cessation, nor the grasping or the relinquishing, nor the defilement or the purification, nor the accumulation or the diminution, nor the decrease or the increase of the powers, the grounds of self-confidence, the analytical knowledges, the unique qualities of a Buddha, and so on, up to omniscience itself. Why is that?

For in this way, venerable Śāriputra, omniscience does not exist by way of its own-being as omniscience. Thus, venerable Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the perfection of wisdom and trains in omniscience for the sake of the non-arising and non-cessation of all phenomena, for their non-apprehension and non-abandonment, for their non-defilement and non-purification, and for neither their accumulation nor their diminution, neither their decrease nor their increase.
"He will go forth by means of a departure that is not a training.
Thus, the path of the pratyekabuddha has been described as reaching the supreme dharmas in that very context.
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the venerable Śāriputra:
"Venerable Śāriputra, from where should the perfection of wisdom be sought?
Śāriputra replied:
"Kauśika, the perfection of wisdom should be sought from the chapter of Subhūti."
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the elder Subhūti:
"It is indeed through your power, noble Subhūti, and through your sustaining grace, that the noble Śāriputra [has spoken thus]."
Thus he speaks:
"Kauśika, the perfection of wisdom is to be sought from the discourse of the venerable Subhūti.
Subhūti said:
"Kauśika, this is not my power; this is not my empowerment.
Śakra asked: "Whose power is this? Whose empowerment is this?
Subhūti replied:

This, Kauśika, is the power of the Tathāgata; this is the sustaining grace of the Tathāgata. Yet, apart from the nature of phenomena which is without sustaining basis, a Tathāgata is not to be found; nor apart from suchness is a Tathāgata to be found.
O Lord of Gods, all phenomena are without sustaining basis.
The Lord of Devas said:
"How, Noble Subhūti, do you speak thus regarding all dharmas which are without a basis?
That this is the power of the Tathāgata, that this is the sustaining grace of the Tathāgata."
Subhūti said:
"So it is, Kauśika, so it is. Apart from the nature of phenomena that is without a basis, a Tathāgata is not to be apprehended."
The Tathāgata is not apprehended apart from suchness;
nor is the Tathāgata apprehended in a dharma-nature that is without a basis; nor is a dharma-nature without a basis apprehended in the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, the Tathāgata is not apprehended in suchness,
nor is suchness apprehended in the Tathāgata;
the Tathāgata is not apprehended in the suchness of form.
Furthermore, the Tathāgata is not apprehended in the suchness of form, nor is the Tathāgata apprehended in the dharmatā of form; nor is the dharmatā of form in the Tathāgata.
Nor is the Tathāgata apprehended in the suchness of feeling, the suchness of perception, the suchness of mental formations, or the suchness of consciousness; nor is he [apprehended therein].
The Tathāgata is perceived in the suchness of consciousness,
but the Tathāgata is not perceived in the dharmic nature of consciousness,
nor is the dharmic nature of consciousness in the Tathāgata.

In this way, with respect to the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, both individually and collectively; with respect to dependent origination; with respect to the perfections, the superknowledges, and the truths;

with respect to the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, and the formless attainments; with respect to all emptinesses, all samādhis, and all doors of dhāraṇī; with respect to the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a Buddha; and so on, up to the suchness of omniscience.
The Tathāgata is not apprehended;
nor is the suchness of omniscience apprehended in the Tathāgata;
nor is the Tathāgata apprehended within the dharmatā of omniscience.
And there is no nature of omniscience in the Tathāgata. Why is that?

Because, Kauśika, the Tathāgata is neither joined with nor disjoined from the suchness of form; he is neither joined with nor disjoined from the suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. Because, Kauśika, the Tathāgata is neither joined with nor disjoined from the true nature of form.
He is neither conjoined nor disjoined with the true nature (*dharmatā*) of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness;

nor is he conjoined nor disjoined with anything other than the suchness (*tathatā*) of form. He is neither conjoined nor disjoined with anything other than the true nature of form. Feeling, perception, and mental formations are neither conjoined nor disjoined with anything other than the suchness of consciousness.

Nor is he joined to or disjoined from anything other than the true nature (*dharmatā*) of consciousness. In detail, up to: that Tathāgata is neither joined to nor disjoined from the suchness of omniscience (*sarvajñatātathatā*), nor is he joined to or disjoined from the true nature of omniscience (*sarvajñatādharmatā*).
Nor is he joined with or disjoined from anything other than omniscience; nor is he joined with or disjoined from anything other than the true nature (*dharmatā*) of omniscience.

For, Kauśika, that which is neither joined with nor disjoined from all phenomena—this is its power, this is its sustaining presence (*adhiṣṭhāna*) by way of the yoga of non-sustaining. Furthermore, Kauśika, as for what you have said:
From where should a bodhisattva mahāsattva seek the perfection of wisdom?
It should not be sought from form, nor sought apart from form;
it should not be sought from feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, nor sought apart from consciousness. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, that which is the perfection of wisdom, and that which is form, and feeling, and perception,
and mental formations, and consciousness, and that which is the search— all these dharmas are neither conjoined nor disjoined;
they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.
Furthermore, Kauśika, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not seek the perfection of wisdom through the elements,

nor through the sense bases, nor through dependent origination, nor through the perfections, nor through the factors conducive to awakening, nor through the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, or the formless attainments.

It is not to be sought from the truths, nor from the superknowledges, nor from the concentrations, nor from the doors of dhāraṇī, nor from the powers, nor from the grounds of self-confidence, nor from the analytical knowledges, nor from the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, up to and including omniscience; it is not to be sought elsewhere than in omniscience itself. Why is that?

For it is thus, Kauśika: that which is the perfection of wisdom, that which is the knowledge of all aspects, and that which is the seeking—all these dharmas are neither conjoined nor disjoined; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, form is not the perfection of wisdom, nor is the perfection of wisdom apart from form; feeling is not [the perfection of wisdom].
Perfection of wisdom is not perception, nor mental formations, nor consciousness; nor is perfection of wisdom elsewhere than in consciousness.

In this way, the aggregates, elements, sense-fields, dependent origination, perfections, truths, superknowledges, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the immeasurables, the meditations, the formless attainments, all the emptinesses, all the samādhis, and all the doors of dhāraṇī—whether taken individually or collectively—are likewise [not the perfection of wisdom, nor elsewhere than in them].

The ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a buddha, up to and including omniscience, are not the perfection of wisdom, nor is the perfection of wisdom other than omniscience. Likewise, the suchness of form is not the perfection of wisdom, nor is the perfection of wisdom other than the suchness of form; it is not the suchness of feeling, not the suchness of perception, and not the suchness of formations.
The suchness of consciousness is not the perfection of wisdom, nor is the perfection of wisdom other than the suchness of consciousness.

The nature of form is not the perfection of wisdom, nor is the perfection of wisdom other than the nature of form; the nature of feeling, the nature of perception, the nature of formations, and the nature of consciousness are not the perfection of wisdom, nor is the perfection of wisdom other than them.

The perfection of wisdom is not the true nature of consciousness, nor is the perfection of wisdom elsewhere than the true nature of consciousness; the perfection of wisdom is not the suchness of omniscience, nor is the perfection of wisdom elsewhere than the suchness of omniscience; the perfection of wisdom is not the true nature of omniscience, nor is the perfection of wisdom elsewhere than the true nature of omniscience. For what reason?

For in this way, Kauśika, all these dharmas do not exist and are not apprehended. Just so, since all dharmas do not exist and are not apprehended, form is not the perfection of wisdom, nor is the perfection of wisdom other than form;

the suchness of form is not the perfection of wisdom, nor is the perfection of wisdom other than the suchness of form; the dharma-nature of form is not the perfection of wisdom, nor is the perfection of wisdom other than the dharma-nature of form.

Neither feeling, nor perception, nor mental formations, nor consciousness is the perfection of wisdom; nor is the perfection of wisdom other than consciousness. Neither the suchness of consciousness is the perfection of wisdom, nor is the perfection of wisdom other than the suchness of consciousness. Neither the true nature of consciousness is the perfection of wisdom.

The perfection of wisdom is not other than the true nature of consciousness (*vijñāna-dharmatā*). In this same way, among the aggregates, elements, sense bases, and dependent origination— whether considered individually or collectively— there are the perfections, the truths, the superknowledges, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations,
the formless attainments, all the emptinesses, all the samādhis, all the doors of dhāraṇī, and the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, and the analytical knowledges.

The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) are not the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), nor is the perfection of wisdom other than the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. The suchness (*tathatā*) of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is not the perfection of wisdom, nor is the perfection of wisdom other than the suchness of the knowledge of all aspects. The true nature (*dharmatā*) of the knowledge of all aspects is not the perfection of wisdom, nor is the perfection of wisdom other than the true nature of the knowledge of all aspects.
Thus, with reference to the path of seeing along with its benefits, there is the receptivity to the dharma-knowledge regarding suffering.
Then, Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the venerable elder Subhūti:
"Venerable Subhūti, this perfection of wisdom is a great perfection for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas."
This perfection of wisdom, Venerable Subhūti, is an immeasurable perfection; this perfection of wisdom is an infinite perfection; this perfection of wisdom is an endless perfection.
By training in this, stream-enterers have attained the fruit of stream-entry; likewise, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas have attained pratyekabodhi.
By bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) has been attained and unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) has been fully realized.
"He has fully awakened and he will fully awaken.
Subhūti said: "So it is, Kauśika, so it is."

This perfection of wisdom is the great perfection, this is the immeasurable perfection, this is the boundless perfection, this is the infinite perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas— namely, the perfection of wisdom—
in which those training have attained the fruit of stream-entry;
likewise, by those who are once-returners, non-returners, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas, individual enlightenment has been attained.

By means of the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas, the knowledge of all aspects has been attained, supreme perfect enlightenment has been fully awakened to, is being fully awakened to, and will be fully awakened to. For what reason?
Because of the greatness of form, Kauśika, this is the great perfection of the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas. And for what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no prior limit of form is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended;
and because of the greatness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, Kauśika, this is the great perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no [prior limit] of consciousness is apprehended.
The prior limit is not apprehended, the subsequent limit is not apprehended, and the middle is not apprehended. In this same way, [the prior, subsequent,

and middle limits] are not apprehended for the factors of dependent origination— whether taken individually or collectively— for the perfections, the truths, the superknowledges, the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening, the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, the formless attainments, all the emptinesses, all the samādhis, and all the doors of the dhāraṇīs.

Because of the greatness of the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four grounds of self-confidence, the four analytical knowledges, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and so on up to the greatness of the knowledge of all aspects— Kauśika, this is the great perfection of the bodhisattvas,
the mahāsattvas. For what reason is that?

For in this way, Kauśika, no prior limit of omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) is apprehended, no subsequent limit is apprehended, and no middle is apprehended. By this method, Kauśika, this is the great perfection (*mahāpāramitā*) of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas.
Thus is the knowledge of phenomena regarding suffering (*duḥkhe dharmajñāna*).
Because form is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection is immeasurable for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of form is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.

In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of form is apprehended. Because space is immeasurable, form is immeasurable; and because form is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is immeasurable. Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is immeasurable. For what reason is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of consciousness is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.

In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of consciousness is apprehended. Due to the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of consciousness; and due to the immeasurability of consciousness, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Thus it is with the aggregates, elements, sense-fields, factors of dependent origination, perfections, and factors conducive to awakening, whether taken individually or collectively.

Kauśika, because the truths, the superknowledges, the measures, the meditations, the formless attainments, all the emptinesses, all the samādhis, all the doors of dhāraṇī, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, the unique buddha-dharmas, up to the knowledge of all aspects are immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is an immeasurable perfection. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the knowledge of all aspects is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.

In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is apprehended. Because space is immeasurable, the knowledge of all aspects is immeasurable; and because the knowledge of all aspects is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is immeasurable. By this method, Kauśika, this perfection of the immeasurable belongs to the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. Thus is the receptivity to the subsequent knowledge regarding suffering (*duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ*).
Kauśika, because form is immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of form is apprehended.

Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of form cannot be apprehended. Due to the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of form; and due to the immeasurability of form, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. In this same way, it should be stated up to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). This is the subsequent knowledge regarding suffering (*duḥkhe 'nvayajñāna*).
"Kauśika, because form is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?

Because neither an end nor a middle of form is apprehended. Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite.
Why is that?"

For in this way, Kauśika, neither the end nor the middle of consciousness is apprehended. Likewise, among the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields, both individually and collectively; among dependent origination, the perfections, the superknowledges, and the truths; among the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path; among the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, and the formless attainments; among all the emptinesses, all the samādhis, and all the doors of dhāraṇī; and among the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a Buddha—[none of these have an end or a middle that can be apprehended].
Kauśika, because omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of omniscience is apprehended. It is by this method, Kauśika, [that it is so].

This perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite, based on the infinitude of form, up to and including the infinitude of the knowledge of all aspects. Thus is the negation of the cause.
Furthermore, Kauśika, because its objective referent is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas—namely, the perfection of wisdom—is infinite.
The Lord of Devas said:
"Venerable Subhūti, how is it that through the infinity of objective referents (*ālambana*), this perfection of wisdom—the perfection of wisdom of the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas—is infinite?
Subhūti replied:

Because the objective referents (*ālambana*) of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas—namely, the perfection of wisdom—is infinite. This is the negation of origination (*samudaya-pratiṣedha*).
Furthermore, Kauśika, because the objective referents are infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas—namely, the perfection of wisdom—is infinite.
Devendra said:

"Venerable Subhūti, how is it that this perfection of wisdom— the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas— is an infinite perfection by virtue of the infinitude of its objective referents?
Subhūti replied:
"Because the objective support of the *dharmadhātu* is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas—namely, the perfection of wisdom—is infinite. Thus is the negation of arising.
Furthermore, Kauśika, because the objective support of *tathatā* is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas—namely, the perfection of wisdom—is infinite.
Devendra said:
"Venerable Subhūti, how is it that this perfection of wisdom—the perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas—is infinite because of the infinitude of the object of focus, namely suchness?
Subhūti replied:
"For indeed, Kauśika, because suchness is infinite, the object of focus is infinite."
Thus, because suchness as an object is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas—namely, the perfection of wisdom—is infinite. This concludes the negation of conditions.
Furthermore, Kauśika, because sentient beings are infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas—namely, the perfection of wisdom—is infinite.
Devendra said:
"Venerable Subhūti, how is it that because of the infinity of sentient beings, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas—the so-called perfection of wisdom—is infinite?
Subhūti replied: "What do you think?"
"Kauśika, of what dharma is this a designation, namely 'being,' 'being'?
Devendra said:
"Venerable Subhūti, this is not a designation for a dharma; it is an adventitious name that has been superimposed."
"This designation 'sentient being,' 'sentient being' is a designation that has been superimposed without a real basis; it is a designation that has been superimposed without an objective referent.
Subhūti said:
"What do you think, Kauśika, has any indication of a 'sentient being' been made here in this perfection of wisdom?
Devendra said:
"No, Venerable Subhūti."
Subhūti said:

"Kauśika, where no indication of a 'being' has been made, there is no such thing as the infinity of beings. If, Kauśika, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha were to remain for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā, [and were to declare] 'being, being'..."
Thus one should speak these words. What do you think, Kauśika, is there any being therein who has been born or who has ceased?
Devendra said:
No, Venerable Subhūti. Why is that?
Because a sentient being is pure from the very beginning.
Subhūti said:

"Kauśika, by this method, one should understand that because sentient beings are infinite, the perfection of wisdom is infinite. Thus, in that very context, he illuminates the fact that [the perfection of wisdom] has the realm of sentient beings as its objective; this is the receptivity to the knowledge of phenomena regarding the origin [of suffering]. Then, indeed, the gods together with Indra, together with Brahmā, together with Prajāpati, along with the hosts of women, men, and sages, uttered this inspired utterance three times:
Oh, what Dharma!
Oh, what Dharma!
Oh, the true nature of Dharma, which is being taught by the Elder Subhūti through the power of the Tathāgata!

Through the empowerment of the Tathāgata, it is indicated, manifested, and revealed: "Blessed One, we shall uphold those very Bodhisattvas, Mahāsattvas, who shall not be separated from this perfection of wisdom;
yet, indeed, no dharma whatsoever is apprehended—whether form, feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, up to and including omniscience."
"How much less, then, can the establishment of the three vehicles be discerned—whether it be the vehicle of the śrāvaka, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddha, or the Great Vehicle?
Then the Blessed One addressed those sons of the gods:
"So it is, sons of the gods; so it is."

Just as you speak these words, not even a single dharma is apprehended—whether it be form, feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, up to and including omniscience—and yet the establishment of the three vehicles is discerned:
namely, the vehicle of the śrāvakas, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, or the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna). Thus it is with the Tathāgata.
O sons of the gods, that bodhisattva mahāsattva who is not separated from this perfection of wisdom through the yoga of non-apprehension should be upheld. Why is that?

Because herein, within this perfection of wisdom, the three vehicles—the vehicle of the śrāvakas, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, or the Great Vehicle—are taught in detail. And it is not apart from the perfection of generosity...

The Tathāgata is not apprehended apart from the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, or the perfection of meditative concentration; nor is the Tathāgata apprehended apart from the perfection of wisdom. Nor is he apprehended apart from internal emptiness, nor apart from [external emptiness].

The Tathāgata is not perceived apart from external emptiness, nor apart from internal-external emptiness, up to and including apart from the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature. The Tathāgata is not perceived apart from the applications of mindfulness. Likewise, he is not perceived apart from the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, the path, the superknowledges, the truths, the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, the formless attainments, the concentrations, or the doors of dhāraṇī.
A Tathāgata is not apprehended. Nor is a Tathāgata apprehended apart from the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a Buddha.

Nor is a Tathāgata apprehended apart from the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). And, O sons of gods, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas train in all these very dharmas, beginning with the perfection of generosity.

...up until they train in the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). Therefore, O sons of the gods, that bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices without being separated from this perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) should be called a Tathāgata himself.
O sons of the gods, when I was in the presence of the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Dīpaṃkara—
In the capital city of Dīpavatī, while standing in the midst of the crossroads, may I never be separated from the perfection of generosity.

Likewise, may I never be separated from the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, may I never be separated from internal emptiness; likewise, may I never be separated from external emptiness and internal-external emptiness.
May I never be separated from the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature. Likewise, may I never be separated from the applications of mindfulness;

likewise, may I never be separated from the right efforts, the bases of miraculous power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path; likewise, [may I never be separated] from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

"May I never be separated from great loving-kindness, great compassion, and the other immeasurable qualities of a Buddha, and may that be through the application of non-apprehension. Then, O sons of gods, I was prophesied by that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha:
'In the future, after incalculable eons, you shall become Śākyamuni in this very Sahā world-system.'"

The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One— named [Nāma].
This is the knowledge of phenomena regarding the origin [of suffering].
Then those sons of the gods said this to the Blessed One:

"It is marvelous, Blessed One, how far this perfection of wisdom assists bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, toward all-aspect omniscience, by means of the yoga of neither grasping nor abandoning form; and by means of the yoga of neither grasping nor abandoning feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness."
Thus [it applies] to the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields, both individually and collectively; to the factors of dependent origination; to the perfections;
to the applications of mindfulness, right efforts, bases of psychic power, faculties, powers, limbs of awakening, and the path;

to the meditative concentrations, formless attainments, all emptinesses, all samādhis, and all doors of dhāraṇī; and to the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

...up to "by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment through the knowledge of all aspects"— this concludes the second chapter, titled "Śakra," in the Noble *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā*,
purified according to the *Abhisamayālaṃkāra*. Then,
the Blessed One addressed the fourfold assembly— monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen— and the bodhisattvas.

Having established all the great beings, the four great kings, the gods of the Cāturmahārājakāyika realm, and so on up to the gods of the Akaniṣṭha realm— all who had gathered and were seated— as witnesses, he addressed Śakra, the lord of the gods, as follows:

Whosoever, Kauśika— be they bodhisattvas mahāsattvas, monks or nuns, laymen or laywomen, sons of noble family or daughters of noble family, or sons of gods or daughters of gods— shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, cultivate, and extensively proclaim this perfection of wisdom to others.
Those who will attend to it properly and those who will not be separated from the mind of omniscience—neither Māras nor the hosts of Māra will find an opportunity to harm them. Why is that?

Because those sons of good family and daughters of good family will have firmly established the very emptiness of form. Likewise, they will have firmly established the very emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
It will be so. For what reason?
Because emptiness does not find entry into emptiness, nor does the signless find entry into the signless.

The wishless does not find an entry-point into the wishless. In this way, the emptiness of the aggregates, elements, sense-bases, and dependent origination—both individually and collectively—will be well-sustained. In this way, the emptiness of the perfections, truths, superknowledges, immeasurables, meditative absorptions, and formless attainments will be well-sustained. In this way, the emptiness of all emptinesses, all samādhis, all doors of dhāraṇī, the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of miraculous power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path will be well-sustained.
It will be well-established. In this way, even the emptiness of the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a Buddha will be well-established by them.
Up to and including the emptiness of the knowledge of all aspects itself will be well-established by those sons of good family and daughters of good family. For what reason is that?
For emptiness does not find entry into emptiness;
the signless does not find entry into the signless; the wishless does not find entry into the wishless. Why is that?
For their intrinsic nature does not exist, by which they might find an entry point, or in which they might find an entry point.
Or might find an opportunity against them.
This is the receptivity to the subsequent knowledge regarding the origin [of suffering].
Furthermore, Kauśika, neither humans nor non-humans shall find an opportunity against those sons of good family or daughters of good family.

They shall attain it. For those sons of good family and daughters of good family have cultivated loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity toward all sentient beings, and they have done so by way of non-apprehension.
Furthermore, Kauśika, those sons of good family or daughters of good family will not die through the failure to avoid dangerous circumstances. Why is that?

For it is because those sons of good family and daughters of good family, while practicing the perfection of generosity, have attended upon all sentient beings with proper service. Or rather, Kauśika, it is because of those gods among the Cāturmahārājakāyikas,
or the Trayastriṃśas, Yāmas, Tuṣitas, or Nirmāṇaratis in this trichiliocosm.

Or by the sons of the gods belonging to the Paranirmitavaśavartin, Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, or Brahmapārṣadya realms, up to the Akaniṣṭha realm, who have resolved their minds upon unexcelled perfect enlightenment,
yet have not heard this perfection of wisdom, nor taken it up, nor retained it, nor recited it, nor mastered it.
Those sons of the gods should hear, take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and attend to this perfection of wisdom in a systematic manner, never being parted from the mind of omniscience.
This is the subsequent knowledge regarding the origin [of suffering].
Furthermore, Kauśika, those sons of good family or daughters of good family who shall take up this perfection of wisdom...
They will uphold, recite, master, and attend to it with proper mental attention; they will remain never separated from the mind of omniscience (*sarvākārajñatācitta*).
Furthermore, Kauśika, for those sons of good family or daughters of good family who have gone to an empty house, or to an open space, or onto a wrong path, there shall be no fear or paralysis.
Or it will come to pass. For what reason?

Because those sons of good family and daughters of good family have well cultivated internal emptiness through the yoga of non-apprehension, and they have well cultivated external emptiness through the yoga of non-apprehension.

Internal-external emptiness was well-cultivated by means of non-apprehension, up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, which was well-cultivated by means of non-apprehension. Then, at that very moment, those sons of the gods belonging to the assembly of the Four Great Kings,
the Trāyastriṃśa, the Yāma, the Tuṣita, the Nirmāṇarati, the Paranirmitavaśavartin, and so on, up to the Śuddhāvāsa realms, [all gathered].

Those sons of the gods said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, we shall provide constant and continuous protection, shelter, and defense for those sons of good family and daughters of good family who will take up, bear in mind, recite, and master this perfection of wisdom."
They will write it down, attend to it thoroughly, and remain never separated from the mind of omniscience.
For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, it is by depending upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the hells are cut off.

The animal realm, the world of Yama, the hosts of asuras, human poverty, calamities, and misfortunes— all these are utterly cut off. It is by relying on the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the manifestation of the ten paths of wholesome action occurs in the world,
as well as the four meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), and the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*).

The perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditation, and the perfection of wisdom will appear in the world; the emptiness of the internal, the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of both the internal and the external, up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, will appear in the world; and the four foundations of mindfulness [will appear].
Of the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers,
the seven factors of enlightenment, the noble eightfold path, the four noble truths, the four immeasurables,
the six supernormal knowledges, the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four grounds of self-confidence, and the four analytical insights.

The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha will appear in the world. Many samādhis, many doors of dhāraṇī, omniscience, and the path of the bodhisattva will appear in the world. Furthermore, it is by depending upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the great kṣatriya clans are known in the world.
In the world, great brahmin families are known; great householder families are known;
and great universal monarch families are known.

The sons of the gods belonging to the retinue of the Four Great Kings are known to exist in the world. Likewise, the sons of the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa, Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmitavaśavartin heavens;
the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, and Brahmapārṣadya gods; the Mahābrahmans; and so on up to the Akaniṣṭha gods are known to exist in the world.

Furthermore, it is by depending upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the fruit of stream-entry is known, and the stream-enterer is known. Likewise, the fruit of once-returning and the once-returner, the fruit of non-returning and the non-returner, arhatship and the arhat in the world are known;
and solitary awakening and the solitary buddhas in the world are known.
Furthermore, it is by depending on the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the maturation of sentient beings is known, the purification of the buddha-field is known,
and the Tathāgata, the Arhat, [is known].
The perfectly awakened one is known in the world; the turning of the wheel of Dharma is known;
the jewel of the Buddha is known.

The Jewel of the Dharma is made known, and the Jewel of the Saṅgha is made known. By this method, O Blessed One, protection, defense, and guardianship should be provided for the bodhisattva mahāsattva by the world with its gods, humans, asuras, gandharvas, yakṣas, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to Śakra, the lord of the gods: "So it is, Kauśika, so it is!
It is by relying upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the realms of hell, the animal realm, and the world of Yama, as well as the [other] destinies, are cut off."

The poverty of gods, the poverty of humans, calamities, and misfortunes— all are completely eradicated. By relying upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva, there occurs in the world the manifestation of the ten paths of wholesome action,
the ten perfections, the ten bodhisattva stages, the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, the formless attainments, and the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening.

The manifestation in the world of the dharmas, the truths, the superknowledges, all the emptinesses, all the meditative concentrations, and all the gateways of the dhāraṇīs occurs by depending upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva. The manifestation in the world of the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, the unique buddha-dharmas, and the knowledge of all aspects occurs by depending upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva. [Likewise] the great kṣatriya clans...
It is by depending upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva that the great śāla-like families of brahmins and the great śāla-like families of householders become known in the world;
the royal families of universal monarchs (cakravartin) become known in the world;
and the sons of the gods from the Cāturmahārājakāyika realm up to the Akaniṣṭha realm become known.

The fruit of stream-entry and the stream-enterer, likewise the fruit of once-returning and the once-returner, the fruit of non-returning and the non-returner, arhatship and the arhat are known in the world;
pratyekabodhi and the pratyekabuddhas are known in the world.
Depending upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva, the maturation of sentient beings is made known, the purification of the buddha-field is made known,
and the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is made known in the world.
The turning of the wheel of Dharma is known in the world;

it is by depending upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva that the appearance of the Jewel of the Buddha, the Jewel of the Dharma, and the Jewel of the Saṅgha occurs in the world. Therefore, Kauśika, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva [is honored] by the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.
He should be honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by the world; and one must constantly and continuously provide him with protection, shelter, and defense.
Kauśika, he who considers this perfection of wisdom to be worthy of honor, reverence, esteem, and worship, should likewise consider the bodhisattva mahāsattva to be worthy of honor and reverence.

Therefore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva should be honored by the world including its gods, and constant, uninterrupted protection, defense, and guardianship should be provided for him. And, Kauśika, if some son of good family or daughter of good family were to honor this trichiliocosm great thousandfold world-system filled with Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas— just as, for example, a grove of sugarcane, or a grove of reeds, or a grove of bamboos, or a grove of *śara* grass, or a grove of rice, or a grove of sesame— [and were to honor it]...
One should honor, revere, and worship him;

yet, whoever honors, reveres, and worships a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has first generated the mind of awakening and is not separated from the six perfections, this person generates far more merit than that.
For what reason does he generate more merit?
It is because, Kauśika, it is not by depending on the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas that bodhisattvas, tathāgatas, arhats, and perfectly enlightened ones are known in the world;
rather, it is by depending on the bodhisattva mahāsattva that śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, tathāgatas, arhats, and perfectly enlightened ones are known in the world.

Therefore, Kauśika, the world with its gods, humans, and asuras should constantly and continuously honor, revere, respect, and worship the bodhisattva mahāsattva, and should provide for him protection, defense, and guardianship.
This is the receptivity to the knowledge of the dharma regarding cessation (*nirodhe dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ*).
Then Śakra, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One:

“It is wonderful, Blessed One, how these bodhisattva mahāsattvas, while taking up, mastering, retaining, reciting, and properly attending to the perfection of wisdom, acquire these qualities pertaining to the present life.”
They bring sentient beings to maturity and purify the buddha-fields;
they travel from buddha-field to buddha-field to attend upon the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones,
and with whatever roots of merit they might desire to honor those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, with those they shall honor them.

And for them, that very thing succeeds in exactly that way. Furthermore, whatever Dharma they hear while standing in the presence of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, that Dharma does not fade from their memory until they have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. Thus, they take hold of excellence of lineage, excellence of mother, and excellence of retinue.
And they take hold of the perfection of the marks, the perfection of radiance, the perfection of the eyes, the perfection of the voice, the perfection of meditative concentration,
and the perfection of the dhāraṇīs. Through skill in means,
having manifested themselves as the body of a Buddha, they travel from world-system to world-system.
Wherever there is no arising of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, they go there and speak in praise of the perfection of generosity.

Likewise, they speak in praise of the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom. They speak in praise of internal emptiness; likewise, they speak in praise of external emptiness and internal-external emptiness.

They speak in praise of the emptiness of non-existence and essential nature; they speak in praise of the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*); they speak in praise of the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) and the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*).

They speak in praise of the applications of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*); likewise, they speak in praise of the right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*), the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*), the faculties (*indriya*), the powers (*bala*), the factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*), and the noble eightfold path (*āryāṣṭāṅgika-mārga*).

They speak in praise of the four noble truths, the superknowledges, the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the grounds of self-confidence, the analytical knowledges, and so forth, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. Through skill in means, they teach the Dharma and discipline sentient beings by means of the three vehicles.
By means of the Śrāvaka vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, and the Buddha vehicle. This is the knowledge of phenomena regarding cessation.
Then, Śakra, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One:
"It is marvelous, Blessed One, how all the perfections are encompassed by this profound perfection of wisdom."

They become fully embraced; namely, the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, the perfection of wisdom;
all the factors conducive to awakening; all samādhis; all gateways of dhāraṇī; all the emptinesses;
the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, and the formless attainments; the truths, the superknowledges, the ten powers, and the grounds of self-confidence.

The analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*), as well as the aggregates, elements, sense bases, and links of dependent origination—both individually and collectively—are thereby encompassed. The fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*) is encompassed;
likewise, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, arhatship, solitary enlightenment (*pratyekabodhi*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are encompassed.
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to Śakra, the lord of the gods:

"By the perfection of wisdom being embraced, all the perfections are embraced. In the same way, all the factors conducive to enlightenment, all the meditative concentrations, all the doors of dhāraṇī, all the modes of emptiness, and the immeasurables, the dhyānas, and the formless attainments [are embraced]."

The superknowledges of truth, all the wholesome paths of action, the ten powers, the four grounds of self-confidence, the four analytical knowledges, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and so on, up to the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields both individually and collectively, the factors of dependent origination,
and even up to the knowledge of all aspects— these are all fully embraced.

Furthermore, Kauśika, listen to those qualities which a son of good family or a daughter of good family attains in this very life through the perfection of wisdom—having taken it up, retained it, recited it, mastered it, written it down, and attended to it with wise reflection. Listen well and pay close attention; I shall speak to you. "So be it, Blessed One," [he replied].
Thus Śakra, the lord of the gods, replied to the Blessed One, and the Blessed One said this: "Kauśika,

if any member of another sect— whether a son of good family or a daughter of good family, or Māra, or a deity belonging to Māra’s host, or an arrogant person— should desire to alienate a bodhisattva mahāsattva from this perfection of wisdom..."
He will desire to dispute, he will desire to quarrel, and he will desire to oppose.
For those who desire to separate, who desire to dispute, who desire to quarrel, and who desire to oppose, whatever quarrels, disputes, and oppositions arise will quickly vanish again;
the intentions of those who desire to separate, who desire to quarrel, who desire to dispute, and who desire to oppose will not reach fulfillment. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, for a long time the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has practiced the perfection of generosity.
Thus, by one practicing the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditation, and the perfection of wisdom,

all internal and external phenomena for the sake of which sentient beings have for a long time fallen into strife, disputes, and opposition are renounced at all times. For the sake of those [sentient beings] for whom, over a long period...

Sentient beings fall into immorality; for their sake, the bodhisattva mahāsattva, having relinquished internal and external phenomena, establishes those sentient beings in ethical discipline. For the sake of those sentient beings who for a long time have fallen into anger, malice, and violence, the bodhisattva mahāsattva, having relinquished internal and external phenomena, [establishes them...]

He establishes them in patience. For the sake of those beings who for a long time have fallen into laziness, the bodhisattva mahāsattva, having relinquished internal and external phenomena, establishes those beings in the perfection of vigor. For the sake of those beings who for a long time have fallen into distracted minds, the bodhisattva...
The Mahāsattva, having relinquished internal and external phenomena, establishes those beings in meditative concentration (*dhyāna*).
For the sake of those beings who have fallen into a state of impaired wisdom (*dauṣprajñā*) for a long night, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,
having relinquished internal and external phenomena, establishes those beings in the perfection of great wisdom (*mahāprajñāpāramitā*).
For the sake of those beings, Kauśika, who have wandered for a long time in saṃsāra due to the obsessions of attraction and aversion,
the bodhisattva mahāsattva,
through skill in means, disciplines those beings and establishes them in the four dhyānas; he establishes them in the four immeasurables and in the four formless attainments.

He establishes them in the four foundations of mindfulness. Likewise, he establishes them in the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the grounds of self-confidence, and the noble eightfold path; in emptiness, the signless, and the wishless; and in the gateways to meditative concentrations and dhāraṇīs.
He establishes them in the four noble truths, the superknowledges, the ten powers, the grounds of self-confidence, and the analytical knowledges.

He establishes them in the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*aṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharma*). He establishes them in the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*), the fruit of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmiphala*), the fruit of non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*), and arhatship (*arhattva*). He establishes them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment (*pratyekabodhi*). He establishes them in unsurpassed, perfect, complete enlightenment (*anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi*). These, Kauśika, are the deeds of a bodhisattva mahāsattva on the bodhisattva path.
While practicing, the virtuous qualities and benefits will be seen; and in the future life, he will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

Having set in motion the wheel of Dharma and established sentient beings according to their aspirations, he will lead them to final nirvana in the realm of nirvana without remainder. These, Kauśika, are the future benefits for a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
There will be these qualities and benefits. Thus is the receptivity to the subsequent knowledge regarding cessation.

Furthermore, Kauśika, in whatever region of the earth sons of good family or daughters of good family shall take up this perfection of wisdom, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, and attend to it properly with right reflection—
In that place, neither Māras, nor deities belonging to the host of Māra, nor followers of other sects, nor wandering mendicants,

nor conceited individuals will be able to cause distraction of mind for the sake of contending with, disputing over, or opposing this perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, they shall obtain further qualities and benefits, namely those arising from this [perfection of wisdom].
By hearing the *prajñāpāramitā*, they will, through the three vehicles in due order, go forth and bring an end to suffering.

It is just as if, Kauśika, there were a medicinal herb called *maghī*; and therein, some creature of the animal kingdom might be seen by a venomous snake that was hungry, seeking food, and searching for nourishment.
Desiring to devour that creature once more, he pursued it. Then, that creature approached the medicinal herb named Maghī; thereupon, the venomous snake turned back at the mere scent of that herb.
For what reason?
For it is thus: the medicinal quality of that herb is such that it overcomes the poison of that venomous serpent.

So powerful, Kauśika, is that herb; even so, Kauśika, whichever son of good family or daughter of good family shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom—

And he will attend to it. In that regard, Kauśika, whatever disputes, quarrels, or conflicts arise, they will, through the splendor of the perfection of wisdom and by the power of the perfection of wisdom, quickly vanish and be pacified;
from wherever they arise, right there they shall disappear, they shall not increase, but shall be pacified.
This is the subsequent knowledge regarding cessation.
For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, the perfection of wisdom brings all phenomena to rest; it does not cause them to increase.
Of which phenomena?

Namely, it is the pacifier and not the increaser of passion, hatred, delusion, ignorance, formative forces, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, mental distress, and despair; it is the remover of the entire aggregate of suffering, as well as the hindrances, obstructions, latent tendencies, and active outbursts.
From the view of a self, the view of a sentient being, the view of a living soul, the view of a nourisher, the view of a person, the view of a spirit, the view of a human, the view of a man,

the view of an agent, the view of an experiencer, the view of a knower, the view of a perceiver, the view of annihilation, the view of eternalism, the view of existence, the view of non-existence— up to all views that have been fabricated, as well as envy, immorality, malice, and indolence.
of distraction, of faulty wisdom, of the notions of permanence, of pleasure, of self, and of purity; of the notion of beauty; of the discursive movements of craving;

of the grasping at form, the grasping at feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; of the grasping at the perfection of generosity, the grasping at the perfection of ethical discipline, the grasping at the perfection of patience, the grasping at the perfection of vigor, the grasping at the perfection of meditation, the grasping at the perfection of wisdom, and the grasping at internal emptiness.

of the grasping at external emptiness, of the grasping at internal-external emptiness, up to the grasping at the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; of the grasping at the applications of mindfulness, of the grasping at the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment; of the grasping at the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, and the formless attainments; of the grasping at the truths and the superknowledges; of the grasping at all the doors of concentration and dhāraṇī; and of the grasping at the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a Buddha.

It is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at omniscience and the grasping at nirvāṇa. This is the receptivity to the knowledge of phenomena regarding the path (*mārge dharmajñānakṣānti*).

Then, indeed, those great kings who are world-protectors (*lokapāla*) in this triple-thousand great thousandfold world system, Śakra the lord of gods, and those Brahmās, including Brahmā Sahāpati, up to the sons of the gods of the Akaniṣṭha heaven—
They will constantly and continuously provide protection, defense, and guardianship for that bodhisattva mahāsattva,

wherever a son of good family or a daughter of good family shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, write down, cause to be written down, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, those who— among the ten directions— ...

In all directions, the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, dwell, remain, and maintain themselves; they too will provide protection, defense, and guardianship for that son of good family or daughter of good family who shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, write, cause to be written, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom.
In such a way that he shall not decline from wholesome qualities,

but shall increase in wholesome qualities— namely, he shall increase through the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom, and shall not decline, by means of the yoga of non-apprehension; he shall increase through internal emptiness and shall not decline.

He will not decline. In this way, through external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, and so on up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, he will increase and not decline by means of the yoga of non-apprehension. He will increase and not decline through the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path.
He will increase and not decline through the immeasurables, the dhyānas, and the formless attainments.
By means of the superknowledges, the ten powers, the grounds of self-confidence, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a Buddha,
he will increase and not decline, through the yoga of non-apprehension. By all meditative concentrations and all doors of dhāraṇī,
he will increase and not decline.
To the extent that he will increase in all-knowledge and not decline through the yoga of non-apprehension— this is the knowledge of phenomena regarding the path—
he will become one whose speech is acceptable and measured,
and he will not be overcome by anger.
He will not be overcome by pride,
he will not be stingy, and he will not be envious.
He himself will abstain from taking life,
he will establish others in the abstention from taking life,
and he will speak in praise of abstaining from taking life.
Furthermore, he will speak in praise of and approve of others who abstain from taking life;
he himself will abstain from taking what is not given,
and he will establish others in the abstinence from taking what is not given.
He will speak in praise of abstaining from taking what is not given, and he will also be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who abstain from taking what is not given.
He himself will also abstain from sexual misconduct.
He will establish others in the abstention from sexual misconduct,
he will speak in praise of the abstention from sexual misconduct,
and he will also be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who abstain from sexual misconduct.
He himself will abstain from false speech,
he will establish others in the abstinence from false speech,
and he will speak in praise of abstaining from false speech.
Furthermore, he will speak in praise of and approve of others who abstain from false speech;
and he himself will abstain from slanderous speech,
and will establish others in the abstinence from slanderous speech.
He will speak in praise of abstaining from slanderous speech;
he will also be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who abstain from slanderous speech.
And he himself will abstain from harsh speech.
He will establish others in abstaining from harsh speech,
he will speak in praise of refraining from harsh speech,
and he will also be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who likewise refrain from harsh speech.
He himself will abstain from frivolous speech,
he will establish others in the abstention from frivolous speech,
and he will speak in praise of abstaining from frivolous speech.
Furthermore, he will speak in praise of and approve of others who abstain from frivolous speech;
he himself will abstain from covetousness and will establish others in the abstinence from covetousness.
He will speak in praise of abstaining from covetousness,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who also abstain from covetousness.
He himself will also abstain from ill-will.
He will establish others in the abstention from malice,
he will speak in praise of the cessation of malice,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who likewise abstain from malice.
He himself will abstain from wrong view,
he will establish others in the abstention from wrong view,
and he will speak in praise of abstaining from wrong view.
Furthermore, he will speak in praise of and approve of others who abstain from wrong views;
and he himself will be established in the perfection of generosity.

He will establish others in the perfection of generosity and will speak in praise of the perfection of generosity. He will also be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who practice the perfection of generosity. And he himself will be established in the perfection of ethical discipline.
He will establish others in the perfection of ethical discipline,
he will speak in praise of the perfection of ethical discipline,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who also practice the perfection of ethical discipline.
He himself will be established in the perfection of patience, he will establish others in the perfection of patience,
and he will speak in praise of the perfection of patience.
He will also speak in praise of and approve of others who practice the perfection of patience.
He himself will be established in the perfection of vigor,
and he will establish others in the perfection of vigor as well.
He will speak in praise of the perfection of vigor,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who also practice the perfection of vigor.
He himself will be established in the perfection of meditative concentration.
He will establish others in the perfection of meditation,
he will speak in praise of the perfection of meditation,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who also practice the perfection of meditation.
He himself will be established in the perfection of wisdom, he will establish others in the perfection of wisdom,
and he will speak in praise of the perfection of wisdom.
He will also speak in praise of and approve of those others who practice the perfection of wisdom.
He himself will be established in internal emptiness,
and he will establish others in internal emptiness as well.
He will speak in praise of internal emptiness; he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who also cultivate internal emptiness.
He himself will be established in external emptiness, and he will establish others in external emptiness as well.
He will speak in praise of external emptiness;
he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who also cultivate external emptiness.
And he himself will be established in internal-external emptiness.
He will establish others in internal-external emptiness,
he will speak in praise of internal-external emptiness,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others as well who cultivate internal-external emptiness.
He himself will become established in the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, he will establish others in the emptiness of the nature of non-existence,
and he will speak in praise of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence.
He will also speak in praise of and approve of those others who cultivate the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
He himself will enter into all meditative concentrations and will establish others in the attainment of all meditative concentrations.
He will speak in praise of all meditative concentrations and attainments;
he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who likewise enter into all meditative concentrations and attainments.
And he himself will have attained the *dhāraṇīs*.
He will encourage others to attain the dhāraṇīs,
he will speak in praise of the attainment of dhāraṇīs,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who have attained the dhāraṇīs.
He himself will first attain the first dhyāna,
he will establish others in the attainment of the first dhyāna, and he will speak in praise of being established in the first dhyāna.
He will also speak in praise of and approve of those others who enter and dwell in the first dhyāna.
He himself will enter the second dhyāna, and so on up to entering the third dhyāna; he himself will enter the fourth dhyāna, and he will establish others in the fourth dhyāna as well.
He will speak in praise of being established in the fourth dhyāna;
he will also be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who, having attained the fourth dhyāna, dwell therein.
And he himself will enter into the meditative absorption of loving-kindness (maitrī).
He will encourage others to undertake loving-kindness,
he will speak in praise of the concentration of loving-kindness,
and he will [encourage] those others who practice loving-kindness as well.
They will enter into them, and he will speak in praise of them and approve of them.
He himself will enter into the meditative absorptions of compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity,
and he will encourage others to undertake the meditative absorptions of compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.
He will speak in praise of compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity;
he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who likewise enter into the meditative attainments of compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.
And he himself will enter into the sphere of infinite space.

He will encourage others to attain the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space, he will speak in praise of the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space, and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who also attain the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space.

He himself will attain the sphere of infinite consciousness; he himself will attain the sphere of nothingness; and he himself, having attained the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, will dwell therein.
He will also encourage others to attain the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and he will speak in praise of the attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
He will also speak in praise of and approve of those others who dwell having attained the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
He himself will cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness and will encourage others to undertake the cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness.
He will speak in praise of the cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who also cultivate the foundations of mindfulness.
Likewise, he himself will cultivate the four right efforts.
He will personally cultivate the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the noble eightfold path,
and he will also encourage others to undertake the cultivation of the path.
He will speak in praise of the cultivation of the path,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who also cultivate the path.
He himself will cultivate the four noble truths.
He will establish others in the four noble truths,
he will speak in praise of the four noble truths,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who also cultivate the four noble truths.
He will himself cultivate the concentrations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
he will establish others in the cultivation of the concentrations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
and he will speak in praise of the cultivation of the concentrations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
He will also speak in praise of and give his approval to others who cultivate the concentrations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
he himself will attain the eight liberations,
and he will encourage others to attain the eight liberations.
He will speak in praise of the eight liberations,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who attain those same eight liberations.
Furthermore, he himself will personally attain the nine successive meditative absorptions (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*).
He will encourage others to attain the nine successive meditative absorptions (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti),

he will speak in praise of the nine successive meditative absorptions, and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who likewise enter into the nine successive meditative absorptions.

He himself will attain the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four grounds of self-confidence, and the four analytical knowledges; he will encourage others to take up the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four grounds of self-confidence, and the four analytical knowledges,
and he will speak in praise of the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four grounds of self-confidence, and the four analytical knowledges.
Furthermore, he will speak in praise of and approve of others who attain the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four grounds of self-confidence, and the four analytical knowledges.
He himself will attain the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and he will encourage others to take up the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
He will speak in praise of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*),
and he will also be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who shall attain those eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Furthermore, he himself will possess the quality of being non-forgetful (*asaṃmoṣadharman*).

He will encourage others to adopt the quality of non-forgetfulness, he will speak in praise of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who have been established in the quality of non-forgetfulness.
He himself will be established in the knowledge of all aspects, and he will encourage others to take up the knowledge of all aspects and speak in praise of the knowledge of all aspects;

furthermore, for those others who are established in the knowledge of all aspects, he will be one who speaks their praise and gives his approval. This is the receptivity to the subsequent knowledge of the path.

Furthermore, Kauśika, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the six perfections gives a gift, he makes it common to all sentient beings and dedicates it to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by way of non-apprehension. Whatever ethical discipline he maintains, he makes it common to all sentient beings and dedicates it to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

By way of non-apprehension, whatever patience he cultivates, having made it common to all sentient beings, he dedicates it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by way of non-apprehension. Whatever vigor he exerts, having made it common to all sentient beings, he dedicates it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by way of non-apprehension. Whatever meditative concentration he enters...
Having made that common to all sentient beings, he dedicates it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Whatever wisdom he cultivates, having made that common to all sentient beings, he dedicates it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by means of the yoga of non-apprehension. For a son of good family or a daughter of good family who practices in this way, Kauśika...
Or, regarding the six perfections, mindfulness arises in this way: "If I do not give gifts, I will be reborn among families in the miserable states."
"Neither will there be the ripening of sentient beings for me, nor will there be the purification of my buddha-field,
nor shall I attain omniscience. It occurs to him thus:
If I do not guard my moral discipline, the gates to the three miserable destinies will be opened for me, and I shall have no rebirth among gods or humans.
There is no ripening of sentient beings, nor the purification of a buddha-field, much less the attainment of omniscience. It occurs to him:
"If I do not cultivate patience..."
My faculties will be impaired, my facial complexion will become sallow, and I shall not obtain perfection of form.

By whatever perfection of form I may practice the conduct of a bodhisattva, may sentient beings become fixed in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment merely by seeing me; yet, I shall not bring sentient beings to maturity through that perfection of form,
nor shall I purify a buddhafield.
"How much less, then, shall I attain omniscience? It occurs to him:
"If I become indolent, I will certainly not cultivate the path of a bodhisattva."
"I shall not exert vigor; how then shall I fulfill the qualities of a Buddha, let alone attain omniscience?"— to him it occurs thus:
If I should become distracted in mind,
I will not train for the perfection of all meditative concentrations,
nor will I bring sentient beings to maturity.
"I shall not purify a buddha-field;
how then could I ever attain omniscience? It occurs to him:
"If I am to be of poor wisdom..."

"By means of skill in wisdom and expedient means, having transcended the level of the śrāvaka and the level of the pratyekabuddha, having matured sentient beings and purified the buddha-field, I shall train to fully awaken to omniscience"— if one thinks thus, he trains accordingly; it is improper [to think otherwise].
"May this be mine; may I, through the power of stinginess, fail to fulfill the perfection of generosity;
likewise, through the power of immorality, the perfection of ethical discipline; through the power of malice, the perfection of patience; and through the power of laziness, the perfection of vigor."
"By the power of distraction, I would not fulfill the perfection of meditation; by the power of faulty wisdom, I would not fulfill the perfection of wisdom.

Not fulfilling the perfection of generosity, and likewise not fulfilling the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom, I would not emerge into the knowledge of all aspects. For in this way, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family [would abandon] the benefits pertaining to the present life."
And one will obtain the qualities and benefits pertaining to future lives who shall take up, recite, master, propagate, write, cause to be written, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom,
and who shall remain never separated from the mind of omniscience.
Thus, the subsequent knowledge regarding the path has been explained; this concludes the Bodhisattva’s path of seeing.
When this had been said, Śakra, the lord of the gods, addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"It is wonderful, Blessed One, how far this perfection of wisdom stands ready for the taming and the transformation of the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas."
The Blessed One said:
"Furthermore, Kauśika, how is it that the perfection of wisdom is present for the taming and the transformation of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas?
When this was said, Śakra, the lord of the gods, addressed the Blessed One as follows:
In this case, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the mundane perfection of generosity gives gifts to the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, the pratyekabuddhas, and the śrāvakas.

He thinks, "I am giving gifts to the Buddhas, bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas, as well as to the wretched, the destitute, the seekers, and the beggars. Through that gift, he becomes arrogant due to a lack of skillful means. For that bodhisattva mahāsattva...
While guarding mundane ethical discipline, one thinks thus:
"I am practicing the perfection of ethical discipline; I am fulfilling the perfection of ethical discipline."
He becomes conceited because of that. As that bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates worldly patience, it occurs to him:
"I am practicing the perfection of patience; I am fulfilling the perfection of patience."
He becomes conceited because of that. As that bodhisattva mahāsattva exerts mundane diligence, it occurs to him:
"I am practicing the perfection of diligence; I am fulfilling the perfection of diligence."
