All phenomena are understood to be like magical illusions.
Subhūti said:
When bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, do not even conceive of a dream as real, [how much less so other phenomena].
They do not conceive of it as a dream;
they do not conceive of the dream as "mine";
they do not even conceive of it within the dream. In this way, they do not conceive of anything up to and including a magical creation.
They do not conceive of the emanation;
they do not conceive of the emanation as "mine"; nor do they conceive even in the emanation.

At that time, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas have fully understood all phenomena as being like a dream, up to and including all phenomena as being like a magical creation. Thus has been explained the application of the sevenfold higher knowledge (*abhijñā*).
Furthermore, Kauśika, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)...
One does not conceive of form, one does not conceive by means of form, and one does not conceive, "Form is mine."
He does not conceive of form either; he does not conceive of a dream,
he does not conceive by means of a dream,
and he does not conceive, "The dream is mine."
One does not conceive even of a dream, nor as long as one does not conceive of a magical creation,
nor by means of a magical creation.
One does not conceive "this is created by me," nor does one conceive in the created;
one does not conceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
One does not conceive by means of consciousness;
one does not conceive "consciousness is mine";
nor does one conceive in consciousness. In this way, [one does not conceive] the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, both individually and collectively, nor dependent origination.

All the perfections, all the emptinesses, all the samādhis, all the doors of dhāraṇī, the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the dhyānas, the formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative attainments,
emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the superknowledges, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a Buddha.
As long as one does not conceive of omniscience,
does not conceive by means of omniscience,
and does not conceive "omniscience is mine," [one does not fall into conceit].
He does not conceive even of omniscience;
he does not conceive of a dream,
nor does he conceive by means of a dream.
One does not conceive "this is my dream," nor does one conceive even within a dream; likewise,
one does not conceive [anything] up to a magical creation.
One does not conceive of the emanation;
one does not conceive of the emanation as "mine"; nor does one conceive even in the emanation. Thus is described the equality of application.

Then, indeed, through the power of the Buddha, those gods belonging to the assembly of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa, the Yāma, the Tuṣita, the Nirmāṇarati, and the Paranirmitavaśavartin [heavens], as well as the Brahmapārṣadyas, the Brahmapurohitas, and the Mahābrahmans, who were in this great trichiliocosm world-system, [all assembled].

As far as the Śuddhāvāsakāyika gods, they all scattered divine sandalwood powder and approached the Blessed One; having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side.
Then indeed, the four Great Kings, Śakra, Brahmā, and the Śuddhāvāsakāyika gods, through the power of the Buddha, brought to mind a thousand Buddhas.

He was teaching the Dharma using these very same syllables and these very same names, with monks named Subhūti questioning him on this very Perfection of Wisdom; and Śakra, the lord of the gods, was also questioning him on this very Perfection of Wisdom.
In this way, in the eastern direction, the southern, the western, the northern, the zenith, and the nadir—in all directions—a thousand Buddhas were attending to him.

He was teaching the Dharma using these very same syllables and these very same names, with monks named Subhūti asking questions about this very Perfection of Wisdom; and everywhere, Śakras, the lords of the gods, were also questioning him about this very Perfection of Wisdom.
Then the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti:
Subhūti, it is on this very spot of earth that the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, having awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment,
will speak this very Perfection of Wisdom. It is also on this very spot of earth that those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who will appear here in this Fortunate Aeon [will do so].

Having fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, they too will speak this very perfection of wisdom. This concludes the indication that [the Buddhas] bear witness to the sixteen moments of the path of seeing.
Then, the Venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:

"By what aspects, by what marks, and by what signs, O Blessed One, will the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, having fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, [speak this perfection of wisdom]?"
“...will he preach the *prajñāpāramitā*?
The Blessed One said:

“In this regard, Subhūti, after the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, he will not teach the Dharma by saying that form is permanent or impermanent. In this same way...”

He will teach the Dharma that there is neither pleasure nor pain, neither self nor non-self, and that form is neither beautiful nor ugly. He will teach the Dharma that form is neither bound nor liberated.
Likewise, he will teach the Dharma that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither permanent nor impermanent.
Thus he will teach the Dharma that there is neither pleasure nor pain, neither self nor non-self, and that consciousness is neither pure nor impure.

He will teach the Dharma that consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. He will teach the Dharma that form is neither past, nor future, nor present. Likewise, he will teach that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise [neither past, nor future, nor present].

He will teach the Dharma thus: "It is neither past, nor future, nor present. In this way, he will teach it regarding the aggregates, elements, sense-bases, and dependent origination—both individually and collectively;

regarding all the perfections, all the emptinesses, all the samādhis, and all the doors of dhāraṇī; regarding the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, the formless attainments, the eight liberations, and the nine successive meditative attainments.

He will teach the Dharma thus: "Emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the superknowledges, the ten powers, the grounds of self-confidence, the analytical knowledges, the unique qualities of a Buddha, up to omniscience itself—these are neither past, nor future, nor present.
This is the receptivity to the knowledge of the Dharma regarding suffering (*duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ*).
Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:
"But how, Blessed One, will the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, having fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, teach the Dharma?
The Blessed One replied:
He will teach the Dharma that "form is utterly pure, utterly pure";
he will teach the Dharma that "feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are utterly pure, utterly pure.

Likewise, [he will teach] the aggregates, elements, sense bases, dependent origination, the perfections, the emptinesses, the factors of enlightenment, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, and the formless attainments.

He will teach the Dharma, up to the point of saying that the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative attainments, emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the superknowledges, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, the unique qualities of a Buddha, the gateways of concentration and dhāraṇī, and even omniscience itself, are utterly pure and absolutely pure.
Thus, regarding the knowledge of phenomena concerning suffering,
Subhūti said: "O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure."
The Blessed One said:
"Subhūti, because form is utterly pure, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure;
Subhūti, because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are utterly pure, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure. Thus..."

Subhūti, because of the purity of everything up to omniscience— including the aggregates, elements, sense-bases, dependent origination, the perfections, the factors conducive to awakening, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, the formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine successive attainments, emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the superknowledges, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a buddha— the perfection of wisdom is pure. This is the receptivity to the subsequent knowledge regarding suffering (*duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ*).
Subhūti said: "For what reason, Blessed One, is the perfection of wisdom pure because form is pure?"

How is it that through the complete purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, the perfection of wisdom is completely pure? Likewise, [how is it that the perfection of wisdom is completely pure] through the aggregates, elements, sense bases, dependent origination, the perfections, the factors of enlightenment, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, the formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative dwellings, emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the superknowledges, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a Buddha?
"Up to: because omniscience is completely pure, the perfection of wisdom is completely pure?
The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, for form there is no arising and no cessation, no defilement and no purification; this is the complete purity of form."

Subhūti, for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, there is neither arising nor cessation, neither defilement nor purification; this is the purity of consciousness. It is the same for the aggregates, the elements, the sense bases, the factors of dependent origination, all the emptinesses, all the samādhis, all the doors of dhāraṇī, and the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening.

The noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, the formless attainments, the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, the superknowledges, the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—
these have neither arising nor cessation, neither affliction nor purification; this is the purity of the Buddha-qualities.
There is no arising and no cessation, no affliction and no purification of omniscience; this is the purity of omniscience. This is the subsequent knowledge regarding suffering.
Furthermore, Subhūti, through the purity of space, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
Subhūti said:
"But how, Blessed One, is the perfection of wisdom pure through the purity of space?
The Blessed One replied:

"The perfection of wisdom is pure through the purity of form up to omniscience—by way of their non-arising, non-cessation, non-defilement, and non-purification, just like space. This is the acceptance of the knowledge of phenomena regarding the origin [of suffering].
"Subhūti, because it is like space, being unsullied, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure.
Subhūti asked:
"How is it, Blessed One, that the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure because it is like space, being unsullied?"
The Blessed One said:
"Because form, up to and including omniscience, is as stainless as space, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure. This is the knowledge of phenomena regarding the origin [of suffering].
Furthermore, Subhūti, because space is ungraspable, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure.
Subhūti said:
"How, Blessed One, is the perfection of wisdom completely pure because space is ungraspable?
The Blessed One replied:

Because form, up to and including omniscience, is as ungraspable as space, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure. This is the receptivity to the subsequent knowledge regarding the origin [of suffering]. Because it is an expression like space, Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, how is it that the perfection of wisdom is pure because of the non-discursiveness of space?
The Blessed One said:
“Subhūti, just as an echo in space is the sound of duality, even so, Subhūti, because form up to omniscience is non-discursive like space, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
Thus, Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is completely pure because it is the non-discursive expression of space; this is the subsequent knowledge regarding the origin [of suffering].
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, how is it that the perfection of wisdom is pure by virtue of the ineffability of space?
The Blessed One replied:

“Subhūti, there is indeed no expression whatsoever for space. In the same way, Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is pure by virtue of the ineffability of form, up to and including omniscience. Thus it is with regard to cessation.
"The perfection of wisdom is pure because space is non-apprehendable. Subhūti asked:
"How, Blessed One, is the perfection of wisdom pure because space is non-apprehendable?"
The Blessed One said:

"Indeed, Subhūti, there is no apprehension whatsoever of space. In the very same way, Subhūti, because there is no apprehension of anything from form up to omniscience, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure. Thus, Subhūti, because all phenomena are neither produced nor ceased, and because they are neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure."
Subhūti said:
"How, Blessed One, is the perfection of wisdom pure because all dharmas are neither produced nor ceased, and are neither defiled nor purified?
The Blessed One replied:
Because form, up to and including omniscience, is absolutely pure, the perfection of wisdom is completely pure. This is the receptivity to the subsequent knowledge regarding cessation.
Subhūti said:
"Blessed One, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom,"
He shall have no disease of the eye, no disease of the ear, no disease of the nose, no disease of the tongue, no disease of the body, and no disease of the mind.

He shall not be deficient in limb, nor shall his body become decrepit. Furthermore, that son of good family or daughter of good family shall not meet their end through the failure to avoid dangerous circumstances.
Many thousands of deities will follow closely behind them. They are seekers of the Dharma.
The gods of the Four Great Kings up to the gods of the Pure Abodes will follow behind him.

On the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days, a great assembly of deities will gather wherever this son of good family or daughter of good family, a preacher of the true Dharma, shall speak this Perfection of Wisdom. Furthermore, that son of good family...
Or, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family, while speaking this perfection of wisdom, generates much more merit;
he will generate immeasurable, incalculable, limitless, inconceivable, and incomparable merit.
The Blessed One said:
"So it is, Subhūti; so it is.

That son of good family or daughter of good family will generate a much greater merit—immeasurable, incalculable, limitless, inconceivable, and incomparable—who, on the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days, [upholds] this perfection of wisdom."
As he speaks, the assemblies of gods will follow after him. For what reason?
Subhūti, this is a great jewel, namely the perfection of wisdom. This is the subsequent knowledge regarding cessation.
In this regard, Subhūti, when this jewel of the perfection of wisdom is cultivated, it will liberate one from hell.
He will liberate them from the animal realm, he will liberate them from the world of Yama,
and he will liberate them from human poverty; he will cause them to be reborn in the great noble families of kṣatriyas.
He will be reborn among the great brahmin families, he will be reborn among the great householder families,
and he will be reborn among the gods of the Four Great Kings.

As many as will be reborn in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception—this perfection of wisdom is the giver of the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment;
it is the giver of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is that?
Because, Subhūti, herein in this perfection of wisdom the ten paths of wholesome action are taught in detail, wherein they are established, and wherein the great kṣatriya clans are known to arise.
The great śāla clans of brahmins are known;

the great śāla clans of householders are known. The gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa gods, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, and the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods are known;
the Brahmapārṣadya gods are known.
The Brahmapurohita gods are known;
the Mahābrahmā gods are known;
the Parīttābha gods are known.
The gods of Immeasurable Light are known; the gods of Utmost Purity are known; the gods of Limited Virtue are known.
The gods of Immeasurable Purity are known;
the gods of Universal Purity are known.
The Anabhraka gods are known;
the Puṇyaprasava gods are known;
the Bṛhatphala gods are known.
The Śuddhāvāsa gods are known; the Aspr̥ha gods are known;
the Atapa gods are known.
The Sudṛśa gods are known; the Sudarśana gods are known;
the Akaniṣṭha gods are known.
The gods of the sphere of infinite space are known; the gods of the sphere of infinite consciousness are known;
the gods of the sphere of nothingness are known.
The gods of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception are known; the fruit of stream-entry is known,
the fruit of once-returning is known,
and arhatship is known.
Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is discerned;

unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is discerned. For herein, within this perfection of wisdom, the four meditative concentrations are discerned, and the four immeasurables are discerned.
The four formless attainments are known;
the perfection of generosity is known;
the perfection of ethical discipline is known.
The perfection of patience is discerned, the perfection of vigor is discerned,
and the perfection of meditation is discerned.
The perfection of wisdom is known; the perfection of skillful means is known;
the perfection of aspiration is known.
The perfection of power is discerned;
the perfection of knowledge is discerned. The applications of mindfulness are discerned;
the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the factors of awakening, and the path are discerned. Internal emptiness is discerned.
External emptiness is discerned,
internal-external emptiness is discerned, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence is discerned. The four noble truths are discerned,
and the eight liberations are discerned.
The nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling are discerned; emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness are discerned;
the six supernormal knowledges are discerned.
The samādhis are produced;
all the gateways of dhāraṇī are made known;
the ten bodhisattva stages are made known.
The ten powers of a Tathāgata are discerned; the four grounds of self-confidence are discerned;
the four analytical knowledges are discerned.
The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are known; up to and including omniscience is known; and the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, are known.
Three jewels are known: the jewel of the Buddha is known, the jewel of the Dharma is known, [and the jewel of the Saṅgha is known].
The Jewel of the Saṅgha is made known. Since such dharmas as these are taught in detail in this Perfection of Wisdom, it is called the "Jewel Perfection," namely, the Perfection of Wisdom.
Thus, Subhūti, on the path of the Jewel Perfection, no dharma whatsoever arises or ceases, is defiled or purified, is grasped or lost. Why is that?
Because those dharmas which might arise or cease, or which might be defiled, do not exist.

They might be defiled, or they might be grasped, or they might be stolen away. Yet, in this jewel of the perfection of wisdom, not a single dharma arises or ceases— whether it be wholesome or unwholesome, with outflows or without outflows,
blameworthy or blameless, or a state of affliction.

Whether it be free from afflictions (*niḥkleśa*), mundane or supramundane, conditioned or unconditioned—by this method also, Subhūti, this is the perfection of jewels, namely the perfection of wisdom. Thus, regarding the knowledge of phenomena (*dharmajñāna*) on the path:
furthermore, Subhūti, this perfection of jewels would not be defiled by any phenomenon. Why is that?
Because those phenomena by which it might be defiled are not apprehended.
Therefore, Subhūti, this is the jewel-perfection (ratnapāramitā) that is unsullied. This is the receptivity to the subsequent knowledge of the path (mārge ’nvayajñānakṣānti).
Furthermore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, does not even know in this way, nor conceptualize in this way, [then he is truly practicing].
Even thus he does not apprehend anything; even thus he will not engage in conceptual proliferation;
he will course in the perfection of wisdom.
He will cultivate the perfection of wisdom,
he will behold the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones,
and he will travel from buddhafield to buddhafield.

In order to honor, revere, respect, worship, adore, and venerate the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, he will travel from buddha-field to buddha-field, bringing sentient beings to maturity, purifying the buddha-field, and attaining omniscience. This is called the subsequent knowledge regarding the path; thus is the path of seeing described.

Furthermore, Subhūti, this perfection of wisdom does not bring about nor carry away any dharma; it does not show nor indicate; it does not give nor take away; it does not produce nor cause to cease; it is neither annihilating nor eternal; it is neither identical nor diverse; it does not come nor go; it is neither defiling nor purifying; and it does not cause decrease.
It does not cause increase; it is neither past, nor future, nor present. Thus concludes the illumination of the first chapter on omniscience.
Furthermore, Subhūti, this perfection of wisdom neither transcends nor establishes the desire realm, nor does it transcend or establish the form realm.

It neither transcends nor establishes the formless realm; it neither bestows nor discards the perfection of generosity, nor does it bestow or discard the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, vigor, meditative concentration, wisdom, skillful means, aspiration, power, and knowledge. It neither bestows nor discards internal emptiness, nor external emptiness, nor internal-and-external emptiness.

It does not bestow or take away the emptiness of non-existence and essential nature; it does not bestow or take away the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, or the formless attainments; nor does it bestow or take away the four noble truths, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the [three] doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
It neither bestows nor takes away the six superknowledges; it neither bestows nor takes away the ten bodhisattva stages; it neither bestows nor takes away the ten powers of a Tathāgata.

It neither bestows nor takes away the applications of mindfulness; likewise, it neither bestows nor takes away the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, or the path;
it neither bestows nor takes away the powers, the grounds of self-confidence, or the analytical knowledges; and it neither bestows nor takes away the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

She is neither the giver nor the taker of the meditative concentrations (*samādhi*) or the gateways of mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇīmukha*); she is neither the giver nor the taker of the fruit of stream-entry (*srotaāpattiphala*);

she is neither the giver nor the taker of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, arhatship, pratyekabuddhahood, nor omniscience (*sarvajñatā*). Thus ends the second illumination marking the completion of the section on the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*).
Furthermore, Subhūti, this perfection of wisdom neither bestows nor takes away the qualities of a Buddha; it neither bestows nor takes away the qualities of ordinary persons;
it neither bestows nor takes away the qualities of Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.
Nor is it a giver or a taker of the Buddha-qualities, nor a giver or a taker of the conditioned realm. Why is that?
Whether Tathāgatas arise or whether Tathāgatas do not arise, this true nature of phenomena remains established.
The realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), and the fixed order of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*). The Tathāgata fully awakens to this and fully realizes it;
having fully awakened to and fully realized it, he proclaims, teaches, reveals, analyzes, clarifies, and makes manifest.
Then, indeed, many hundreds of thousands of gods, stationed in the sky above, raised shouts of joy and exultation.
They produced divine flowers—blue lotuses, water lilies, white lotuses, red lotuses, and māndārava blossoms—and scattered them. And they spoke these words:

"Aha! We behold this second turning of the wheel of Dharma in Jambudvīpa. As the Perfection of Wisdom was being taught there, many thousands of sons of gods attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Then the Blessed One addressed the Elder Subhūti:

"Subhūti, this is not a second turning of the wheel of Dharma, nor is it the first; nor has this perfection of wisdom appeared for the sake of turning forward or turning back any dharma whatsoever. For what reason?"
"Based on the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Subhūti said:
"Lord, what is this emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, such that this perfection of wisdom does not stand for the sake of the production or the cessation of any dharma whatsoever?"
The Blessed One said:

"Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is empty of the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, meditation, vigor, patience, ethical discipline, and the perfection of generosity are empty of the perfection of generosity;

internal emptiness is empty of internal emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, which is empty of the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence."

The applications of mindfulness are empty through the emptiness of the applications of mindfulness. Likewise, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the paths are empty through the emptiness of the paths;
the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, and the formless attainments are empty through the emptiness of the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, and the formless attainments;
and the noble truths are empty through the emptiness of the noble truths.
The eight liberations are empty of the emptiness of the eight liberations;
the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling are empty of the emptiness of the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling;
emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness are empty of the emptiness of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
The six superknowledges are empty because of the emptiness of the six superknowledges;
all meditative concentrations are empty because of the emptiness of all meditative concentrations;
the gateways of mnemonic formulas are empty because of the emptiness of the gateways of mnemonic formulas.
The ten powers are empty through the emptiness of the ten powers; the grounds of self-confidence are empty through the emptiness of the grounds of self-confidence;
the analytical knowledges are empty through the emptiness of the analytical knowledges.
The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are empty by virtue of the emptiness of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
the fruit of stream-entry is empty by virtue of the emptiness of the fruit of stream-entry;
likewise, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, arhatship, pratyekabuddhahood, and omniscience are empty by virtue of the emptiness of omniscience.
Subhūti said:

"O Blessed One, this is a great perfection, namely, the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, the intrinsic nature of all dharmas is empty of the intrinsic nature of all dharmas. And it is by relying on the perfection of wisdom that bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
They awaken perfectly; they do not awaken to any dharma, yet they turn the wheel of Dharma.
They neither turn nor reverse any dharma. No dharma whatsoever is perceived by them, nor is any dharma seen. For what reason is that?
For indeed, all phenomena are not apprehended—those phenomena that either proceed or cease. Why is that?
Because all phenomena are absolutely non-adherent. For emptiness is neither a proponent nor a ceaser; signlessness is neither a proponent nor a ceaser.

The wishless (*apraṇihita*) is neither that which sets [phenomena] in motion nor that which causes them to cease. Such a teaching as this is the illumination, the explanation, the making known, the establishment, the exposition, the analysis, the indication, the clarification, and the full revelation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
This is the completely pure teaching of the perfection of wisdom. And as for this teaching of the perfection of wisdom, it has not been taught by anyone, nor has it been received by anyone.

That has not been realized by anyone. That which has not been realized by anyone—in that, no one has attained final nirvāṇa, nor has anyone been made worthy of offerings (*dakṣiṇīya*) by that teaching of the Dharma.
Thus ends the third illumination marking the completion of the section on the Knowledge of All Aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

This concludes the "Chapter on the Distinctive Practice of the Section on the Knowledge of All Aspects," the third [chapter] in the *Aryapañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Bhagavatī Prajñāpāramitā*, as revised according to the *Abhisamayālaṃkāra*.
